_doc: What each kind of townsperson knows of the realm and the town (systems/npcKnowledge.js). `topics` in the order they speak of them; the first `sure` they know for certain, the rest is hearsay (a band may be off by one, said with a hedge). `places` = how much they know of the land about the town.
hedges: , if the talk at the well is true

sure: I'll tell you how things stand.
hearsay: Well, I only know what I hear.
guarded: I don't say much to strangers.
Not much I care to tell you.

army: barely an army worth the name
the greatest host of any realm

favour._repay: A favour's coin is a loan (mem.owed): repaid within repayDays it warms them by repaidWarmth (late: lateWarmth); asked after past due, they cool by overdueCold once.

wideKnowledge._comment: What townsfolk know of the land about (NpcKnowledge.aboutTown): outlaw lairs within lairRadius, an old place within siteRadius; with expertise places >= wideAt (a guard or traveller, liked enough) they know lairs within wideLairRadius and two old places within wideSiteRadius.

rebuff._doc: Who will not answer the player. Below refuseBelow disposition (or holding a grudge) they always turn the player away; below grudgingBelow, grudgingChance% of the time. Each rebuffed question costs pester disposition. lines by mood (grudge: {victim}); topics add lines for hostile/cold moods per question: news, town, realm, folk, family, people, work.

grudge: After what you did to {victim}? Ask me nothing. Ever.
*spits* You want news? Here's news — {victim} is gone, and it's on you.
I'll tell you nothing. Not for {victim}'s sake, not for coin. Get out.
hostile: Get out of my sight before I call the watch.
Ask me again and see what happens.
I'd sooner talk to a dog.
Clear off. You're not welcome here.
cold: I've nothing to say to you.
*folds arms* Not to you, I don't.
Why would I tell you anything?
Can't you see I'm busy? Go on, off with you.
wary: Don't know, don't care. Ask someone else.
*eyes you* I keep my own counsel with strangers like you.

news: News? Not for the likes of you.
Whatever I've heard, you'll not hear it from me.
town: Find your own way round. I'm no guide for you.
You'll learn this place soon enough — or better, leave it.
realm: Politics is for people I trust. That's not you.
folk: What happens to folk here is no business of yours.
family: Leave my family out of it.
You stay away from my kin, you hear?
people: I don't gossip with the likes of you.
What I think of my neighbours stays between me and them.
work: Help? From you? I'd rather go without.

road._doc: Out on the open road (no town on the hex) — systems/npcKnowledge.js aboutRoad and roadGreeting. Everything said is read from the world: the roadhouse (its name, keeper, rooms, how well it's kept), whose land it is and what kind, where the road runs (traced along the road to the towns it reaches, with the way and the days), outlaws and old places near, and the season. keeper: the one who keeps the house speaks of it as theirs; traveler: where they've come from and where they're bound (the two towns the road joins); anyone else of what they see. {house} {keeper} {town} {from} {to} {dir} {days} {realm} {land} {ruler} {lair} {leader} {site} {rooms} — filled in. days: how a walk is put, by hexes ([max hexes, words]).

keeper: Come in off the road. You'll want a bed, or a bowl, or both.
Shut the door behind you, the wind gets in. Welcome to {house}.
Another one off the road. Sit, sit — there's stew on.
Mind the step. Not many come by this late in the {season}.
traveler: Another soul on the road. Where are you bound?
Well met. Good to see a face that isn't a tree.
Sit if you like. I don't bite.
any: Road-weary, are you? Aren't we all.
*looks you over* You're not from round here. Nobody is, out here.

house: This is {house}. Mine — or the bank's, some winters.
{house}, this is. I've kept it {years} years now.
You're in {house}. {rooms} rooms, a roof that mostly keeps the rain out, and the only fire for miles.

good: The beds are clean and the ale's honest. Folk ride out of their way to stop here.
fair: Nothing fancy, but nobody's died in their sleep. Not lately.
poor: I'll not lie to you — it's seen better days. So have I.

why: Folk walking from {from} to {to} need somewhere to stop. That's all a roadhouse is.
Halfway between {from} and {to}, give or take. That's what keeps the doors open.

journey: I've come up from {from}, bound for {to}. {daysTo} yet, if my feet hold.
On my way to {to}. Left {from} {daysFrom} back.
I'm walking to {to}. Came by way of {from} — wouldn't recommend it.
nowhere: I'm not sure where I'm bound. Away, mostly.

house: {house} — {keeper} keeps it. Decent enough place to break a journey.

realm: This is {realm} land. {ruler}'s, for what that's worth out here.
We're in {realm} — though the crown's men seldom ride this far.
none: No crown holds this stretch. Nobody taxes you out here — and nobody comes when you scream.

terrain.forest: Forest both sides of the road; you can't see ten paces in.
terrain.hills: Hill country. Every mile's uphill, both ways.
terrain.mountains: High country — the passes close when the snow comes.
terrain.plains: Open country. You see weather coming a day off.
terrain.grassland: Open grassland, mile on mile of it.
terrain.swamp: Marsh all round. Stay on the road or the bog has you.
terrain.desert: Dry country. Carry water, whatever they tell you.
terrain.tundra: Cold country. The ground's iron half the year.
terrain.jungle: Jungle pressing in. The road gets narrower every season.
terrain.beach: Close by the sea — you can smell it.

both: The road runs {dirA} to {townA}, {daysA}, and {dirB} to {townB}, {daysB}.
Go {dirA} and it's {townA}, {daysA}. Go {dirB} and it's {townB}, {daysB}. Nothing much between.
one: Follow the road {dirA} and you'll come to {townA}, {daysA}.
off: There's no proper road here. {townA}'s the nearest place, {daysA} {dirA}.

raids: Watch yourself. Riders out of {lair} work this road{leaderBit}. Travel by daylight.
Outlaws out of {lair}, {dir} of here{leaderBit}. They've hit carts on this road.
quiet: They say there's an outlaw camp at {lair}, {dir} of here. Quiet lately. That worries me more.
none: The road's quiet enough. Wolves, now and then.

site: There's {site} {dir}, off the road. People go looking. Not all of them come back past here.

Spring: Spring rains turn the road to soup. Mind the ruts.
Summer: Summer's the busy time — carts and drovers every day.
Autumn: Autumn now. Folk hurry to get where they're going before the snow.
Winter: Winter. Hardly a soul on the road — you're brave or desperate.

days: the best part of a week
